newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Last S.Africans pulled out of Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: Last S.Africans pulled out of Brazzaville.

text.p: Nine South African businessmen have been evacuated from Congo, where fighting entered a sixth day on Tuesday.
"All the people we were aware of are out, that's nine," a South African foreign affairs official told Reuters, adding they had been in the Congo on business.
The official said the men were evacuated with French help to Gabon and were waiting in Libreville for a scheduled flight to Johannesburg on Wednesday.
Pretoria has no diplomatic mission in Congo and the evacuation was coordinated by its staff in Kinshasa, in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire.
South African oil and chemicals firm Sasol Ltd said on Monday it had pulled its four staff out of Congo and they were returning home via Ivory Coast.
Pretoria was keeping in contact with a group of 42 South African farmers in Congo's Niari valley, and was ready to step in if necessary.
"They don't seem to be in any danger but we are in constant contact with them," the official said.
